<b>Лобное брюшко</b> затылочно-лобной мы: The frontal belly of the occipitofrontalis arises from the galea aponeurotica on the top of the skull and blends into the skin of the eyebrows. It raises the brows and folds the forehead into horizontal wrinkles, the look of surprise and attention.
<b>Круговая мышца глаза</b> — кольцо вок: Orbicularis oculi is a ring around the eye opening. Its palpebral part, in the lids, closes them when you blink or sleep; its orbital part, along the rim of the orbit, squeezes the eyes shut and gathers crow's feet at their corners. The lacrimal part helps tears drain.
<b>Мышца, сморщивающая бровь,</b> лежит: Corrugator supercilii lies under the frontal belly and orbicularis oculi, running from the nasal part of the frontal bone to the skin of the mid-brow. It pulls the brows down and together, raising vertical frown lines above the bridge of the nose.
<b>Мышца гордецов</b> — небольшая полоск: Procerus is a small strip on the bridge of the nose, from the nasal bones to the skin between the brows. It pulls that skin down, creasing the bridge of the nose crosswise: a look of threat, distaste or strain.
<b>Носовая мышца.</b> Её поперечная част: Nasalis. Its transverse part runs from the maxilla above the canine over the bridge of the nose to an aponeurosis there and compresses the nostril. The alar part pulls the wing of the nose down and widens the nostril: the flared nostrils of a deep breath or anger.
<b>Мышца, поднимающая верхнюю губу,</b>: Levator labii superioris arises at the lower rim of the orbit, above the infraorbital foramen, and blends into the upper lip. It raises and everts the lip and deepens the nasolabial fold: in disgust, crying and squinting.
<b>Малая скуловая мышца</b> идёт от скул: Zygomaticus minor runs from the zygomatic bone to the upper lip, medial to the major. It lifts the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial fold; it works in a smile and in a sad face.
<b>Большая скуловая мышца</b> — главная: Zygomaticus major is the main smiling muscle: from the zygomatic bone to the corner of the mouth, where it joins the modiolus, a knot where fibers of several muscles meet. It pulls the corner up and out. When it is split in two, a smile shows a dimple.
<b>Мышца смеха</b> — тонкий и непостоянн: Risorius is a thin, inconstant band from the fascia over the parotid gland and masseter to the corner of the mouth. It pulls the corner straight sideways: a wide grin, a bared-teeth grimace, a look of strain.
Orbicularis oris is the core of the lips. Its fibers do not attach to bone; they interlace with other muscles at the corners of the mouth. It closes and presses the lips and purses them; speech, whistling, drinking and keeping food in the mouth depend on it.
<b>Мышца, опускающая угол рта,</b> треуг: Depressor anguli oris is triangular: its broad base arises from the mandible and its apex reaches the corner of the mouth. It pulls the corner down and out: sadness, displeasure, doubt.
<b>Мышца, опускающая нижнюю губу,</b> ид: Depressor labii inferioris runs from the mandible, deep to the triangular depressor, to the skin of the lower lip. It pulls the lip down and out, baring the lower teeth: in disgust, fright and speech.
<b>Подбородочная мышца</b> идёт от альве: Mentalis runs from the sockets of the lower incisors down to the skin of the chin. It raises and wrinkles the chin skin (“orange peel”) and pushes out the lower lip: when hurt, doubtful or about to cry.
<b>Щёчная мышца</b> — основа щеки: от че: Buccinator is the core of the cheek: from both jaws near the molars and from the pterygomandibular raphe to the corner of the mouth. It presses the cheek against the teeth so food does not lodge outside them, and pushes air out when you blow out a candle or play the trumpet.
<b>Подкожная мышца шеи</b> (платизма) —: Platysma, a thin, broad sheet under the skin of the neck: from the skin above the clavicle and chest to the edge of the mandible and the corner of the mouth. It pulls the corners of the mouth down and tenses the neck skin: in fright and great strain.
<b>Улыбка.</b> Большая скуловая мышца тя: Smile. Zygomaticus major pulls the corners of the mouth up and out, zygomaticus minor and levator labii raise the lip, risorius widens the mouth. In a genuine smile the orbital part of orbicularis oculi joins in, and crow's feet gather at the eyes.
<b>Удивление.</b> Лобные брюшка поднимаю: Surprise. The frontal bellies raise the brows, and the forehead folds into horizontal wrinkles. The eyes open wide: the upper lid is lifted not by a facial muscle but by the levator palpebrae superioris, supplied by the oculomotor nerve. The mouth often drops open.
<b>Хмурость.</b> Мышцы, сморщивающие бро: Frown. The corrugators draw the brows together and down, raising vertical lines, and procerus pulls the skin between the brows down, creasing the bridge of the nose crosswise. The orbital part of orbicularis oculi narrows the eyes.
<b>Грусть.</b> Мышцы, опускающие углы рт: Sadness. The depressors pull the corners of the mouth down; mentalis raises the chin skin and pushes out the lower lip. The inner ends of the brows rise (medial fibers of the frontal belly) and draw together (corrugators).
<b>Зажмуривание.</b> Круговые мышцы глаз: Squeezing the eyes shut. Orbicularis oculi contracts as a whole, orbital part included: the lids close tight, the brows come down, and the skin around the eyes bunches into folds. Corrugator, procerus, nasalis and levator labii work with it.
<b>«Трубочка».</b> Круговая мышца рта сж: Pucker. Orbicularis oris presses the lips together and pushes them forward: for whistling, kissing, drinking through a straw. The buccinators press the cheeks against the teeth, and mentalis raises the skin of the chin.
<b>Височная мышца</b> веером начинается: Temporalis fans out from the temporal fossa and temporal fascia; its tendon passes under the zygomatic arch to the coronoid process. Its front fibers raise the jaw, the rear, nearly horizontal ones pull it back. Clench your teeth and you feel it tighten at the temple.
<b>Жевательная мышца</b> — самая сильная: Masseter, the strongest of the four: from the zygomatic arch to the outer surface of the ramus and angle of the mandible. The superficial part runs obliquely back, the deep part almost vertically. It raises the jaw powerfully; clench your teeth to feel it on the cheek.
<b>Медиальная крыловидная мышца</b> — от: Medial pterygoid, from the fossa between the plates of the pterygoid process and the maxillary tuberosity to the inner surface of the angle of the mandible. It raises the jaw and helps protrude it and shift it to the other side. With the masseter it slings the angle.
<b>Латеральная крыловидная мышца</b> идё: Lateral pterygoid runs almost horizontally: the upper head from the greater wing of the sphenoid to the articular disc and capsule, the lower head from the pterygoid process to the neck of the condyle. It protrudes the jaw and starts mouth opening; acting on one side, it shifts the jaw to the opposite side.
<b>Смыкание.</b> Челюсть поднимают височ: Closing. The temporalis, masseter and medial pterygoid raise the jaw. The masseter and medial pterygoid hold the angle of the mandible from both sides like a sling. An adult's bite force at the molars is usually 40–80 kg (90–175 lb).
<b>Открывание.</b> Нижние головки латера: Opening. The lower heads of the lateral pterygoids pull the condyles forward onto the articular eminences, and the muscles under the chin (digastric and other suprahyoids; not shown) lower the jaw. Meanwhile the elevators relax and stretch.
<b>Выдвижение.</b> Обе латеральные крыло: Protrusion. Both lateral pterygoids pull the condyles forward and down along the eminences at once, helped by the medial pterygoids. The lower incisors move ahead of the upper ones. The rear fibers of the temporalis pull the jaw back.
<b>Сдвиг в сторону.</b> Челюсть уходит в: Lateral shift. The jaw moves left: the right condyle slides forward onto the eminence (pulled by the right lateral and medial pterygoids), while the left one turns almost in place about a vertical axis. This is how the teeth grind food.
<b>Жевание</b> — цикл около секунды: чел: Chewing is a cycle of about a second: the jaw drops, swings to the working side, rises with force and, teeth sliding on teeth, returns to the midline. A pattern generator in the brainstem sets the rhythm; receptors in the ligaments of the teeth tune the force.
<b>Височно-нижнечелюстной сустав</b>, ра: Temporomandibular joint, section through the right condyle. The head of the mandible sits in the mandibular fossa of the temporal bone, with the articular eminence in front. Between them is a disc of dense fibrous tissue that splits the joint into upper and lower compartments. Move the slider to open the mouth.
<b>Вращение.</b> В начале открывания (пр: Rotation. Early in opening (up to about 20–25 mm, 1 in, between the incisors) the head turns under the disc like a hinge: the lower compartment works. The condyle barely moves, while the chin drops and swings slightly back.
<b>Скольжение.</b> Дальше латеральная кр: Gliding. Then the lateral pterygoid pulls the head and disc together forward onto the eminence: the upper compartment works. The disc rotates backward relative to the head, and the retrodiscal tissue stretches. The mouth usually opens 40–50 mm (about 2 in).
<b>Мимические мышцы</b> — около двадцати: Muscles of facial expression: about twenty pairs of thin muscles that arise on the facial bones and insert straight into the skin. As they contract, they shift skin, folds, eyelids and lips, and expressions appear. All are supplied by the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII). Pick an expression or click a muscle.
<b>Лицевой нерв</b> (VII пара) выходит и: The facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) leaves the skull through the stylomastoid foramen, enters the parotid gland and splits there into five groups of branches: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular and cervical. Fanning out over the face, they supply all the facial muscles of their side.
<b>Паралич Белла</b> — внезапное поражен: Bell's palsy is a sudden lesion of the facial nerve on one side, often after a viral infection. Half the face is still: the eye will not close, the corner of the mouth droops, the forehead does not wrinkle. Most people recover within weeks or months. In a stroke, by contrast, the forehead usually still moves.
<b>Жевательные мышцы</b> — четыре пары:: Muscles of mastication, four pairs: temporalis, masseter, medial and lateral pterygoids. They arise on the skull, insert on the mandible and move it at the temporomandibular joints. All are supplied by the mandibular nerve (V₃). Pick a muscle or a movement.

\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

The muscles of facial expression develop from the second pharyngeal arch, so all of them are supplied by that arch's nerve, the facial nerve. Unlike skeletal muscles, they lie right under the skin and insert into it at least at one end. Around the eyes and mouth they form ring muscles, while radial ones open these apertures.

The muscles of mastication come from the first pharyngeal arch; they are supplied by the mandibular nerve, the third division of the trigeminal (V₃). The mandible is the only movable bone of the skull, and its two temporomandibular joints always work together.

How it works

Facial muscles do more than show feelings: orbicularis oculi blinks 15–20 times a minute, protecting the eye and spreading tears, and orbicularis oris and the buccinator hold food in place and take part in speech. Basic expressions such as joy, surprise, disgust and fear are understood alike across cultures.

In chewing the jaw traces a loop: it drops, swings to the working side and, as it rises, grinds food between the teeth on that side. The tongue and cheeks keep pushing food back under the teeth, and saliva binds it into a bolus.

Medicine

  • Bell's palsy: sudden weakness of one whole half of the face from a facial nerve lesion; the eye must be protected from drying out. It usually resolves within weeks or months.
  • Central facial palsy (in a stroke) affects the lower half of the face on the opposite side, while the forehead still moves: the upper face receives commands from both hemispheres.
  • TMJ disorder: clicking as the disc slips, pain, limited mouth opening; often linked to bruxism, grinding the teeth during sleep.
  • Jaw dislocation: in a wide yawn the head slips forward past the articular eminence and the mouth will not close; a doctor reduces it by pressing the molars down and back.
  • Trismus, spasm of the chewing muscles so the mouth will not open: with inflammation around a wisdom tooth, with tetanus.
  • Botulinum toxin switches facial muscles off for several months; anti-wrinkle injections rely on this.

Simplifications

  • Muscles are shown as ribbons on a scan of an adult skull; skin, fat and fasciae are removed, and muscle shapes are simplified. The nose is a schematic cartilage shell, and the eyeballs are spheres.
  • Contraction is shown by the muscles shortening and glowing; the facial skin does not deform, and wrinkles are not shown. Each real expression uses more muscles.
  • The mandible is separated from the scan along an arbitrary border (teeth and joints are fused in the scan, cuts are patched); the condyle path and opening angles are averages. The joint section is schematic and enlarged 3.5×.
